articles.title: Infrastructure for the AI era Dynamic capacity management for agents
articles.summary: Google Cloud announced new FinOps controls for Gemini Enterprise to help organizations manage project-level AI spend and eliminate token shock.
articles.detail: The internet connected billions of people and mobile devices, putting computers in every hand. Now, we’re in the middle of the next big technology shift, deploying millions of autonomous AI agents to work alongside employees and end users.

articles.title: FinOps for the AI era New flexible billing and cost controls for agents
articles.summary: Google Cloud announced new FinOps controls to help organizations manage project-level AI spend and eliminate token shock.
articles.detail: To get a real return on AI, financial operations (FinOps) and cost management must evolve alongside technology, giving you clear visibility, proactive cost controls, and flexible payment models that fit your needs.

articles.title: Bringing gVisor sandboxes to distributed Ray clusters
articles.summary: Google Cloud announced support for new games, anti-cheat technologies and increased visual quality on Ray clusters.
articles.detail: The reinforcement learning (RL) ecosystem is rapidly adopting Ray as the unified compute runtime for complex post-training workflows. Across Google Cloud, we see customers using Ray for workloads ranging from multimodal data pipelines to frontier RL.

articles.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Amazon EC2
articles.summary: AWS recognized how it has continued to push the boundaries of what cloud computing can deliver.
articles.detail: On the 20th Anniversary, we recognize how AWS has continued to push the boundaries of what cloud computing can deliver, building custom silicon for general-purpose and AI workloads and expanding EC2 into new form factors and deployment models that our customers in 2006 could not have imagined.

articles.title: Announcing: Aspire 13.5 has shipped
articles.summary: Azure announced the availability of Aspire 13.5, which refreshes the dashboard and aspire.dev.
articles.detail: Aspire 13.5 refreshes the dashboard and aspire.dev, expands the Interaction Service, adds cross-scope Azure references and persistent Kubernetes volumes, and brings live terminals into the apphost.

articles.title: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure 248 and 372 vCPU sizes for D/E v7 series VMs
articles.summary: Azure announced the general availability of new VM sizes powered by Intel Xeon processors.
articles.detail: Azure announces the general availability of 248 and 372 vCPU Dl/D/E v7 VM sizes, powered by Intel Xeon processors. These general-purpose and memory-optimized VMs deliver up to 20% better compute performance than prior-generation Intel-based v6 VMs.

articles.title: Announcing: Extended Support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
articles.summary: Azure announced extended support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server.
articles.detail: Extended Support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server helps you maintain secure, supported workloads while transitioning to newer PostgreSQL versions. articles.title: Retirement: Support for Node 22 LTS ends on April 30, 2027
articles.summary: Azure announced the end of support for Node 22 LTS.
articles.detail: On April 30 2027, support for Node 22 LTS will end. Your apps that are hosted on App Service will continue to run, but security updates will no longer be available, and we’ll no longer provide customer service for Node 22 LTS.

articles.title: Leading Publishers Bring Blockbuster PC Games and Technology to NVIDIA RTX Spark
articles.summary: NVIDIA announced support for new games, anti-cheat technologies and increased visual quality on RTX Spark.
articles.detail: NVIDIA is bringing the next wave of RTX gaming to the Gamescom conference running this week in Cologne, Germany, with support for new games, anti-cheat technologies and increased visual quality. Electronic Arts, Embark and Ubisoft are among the latest game publishers and developers bringing their blockbuster titles to NVIDIA RTX Spark ahead of its launch.

articles.title: How XPUs Meet a World-Class AI Factory
articles.summary: NVIDIA announced its vision for building custom XPUs and full factory solutions for AI.
articles.detail: To generate intelligence at scale, AI factories run continuously, and their economics are defined by delivered output: tokens per second, tokens per watt, cost per token, utilization and uptime. That requires AI infrastructure designed and built as a full factory, not a collection of individual accelerators.

articles.title: With Groq 3 LPX in Full Production, NVIDIA Extends Vera Rubin Inference for Agents
articles.summary: NVIDIA announced the production of its Groq 3 LPX chip and extended its Vera Rubin inference capabilities.
articles.detail: The next era of AI inference won’t be defined by a single breakthrough chip, network or system. It’ll be defined by how every layer of the AI factory works together.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces Jetson Orin Nano 2 Robotics Computer to Redefine Entry-Level Edge AI
articles.summary: NVIDIA announced its new robotics computer for edge AI.
articles.detail: NVIDIA today announced NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 2, a new robotics computer set to redefine entry-level edge AI — putting frontier-class generative AI performance in the hands of millions of developers.

articles.title: The Cognitive Campus Center Journey
articles.summary: Arista Networks announced its vision for building a unified architecture for AI.
articles.detail: For decades, the industry had accepted a status quo plagued by fragile, overly complex, disparate operating systems, rigid hardware controllers, fragmented visibility, and archaic management of siloed three-tier (Access Aggregation Core) designs. We knew there was a better way.

articles.title: Cisco and Nvidia take AI factories from rack to runtime
articles.summary: Cisco and NVIDIA announced their partnership to integrate AI compute systems into Cisco's Secure AI Factory.
